new_candidates.body:
Related: [#2312](https://github.com/StanfordVL/BEHAVIOR-1K/issues/2312). I reproduced a similar failure and isolated an annotation path that remains usable.

**Environment:** OmniGibson 3.9.3, Isaac Sim 5.1.0, Replicator 1.12.27, SyntheticData 0.6.13; Ubuntu 22.04, RTX 5090, driver 575.64.03. Sensor/annotator code is unchanged; local device-placement compatibility patches are present.

**Reproduction:** Load the official [task-0012 / episode_00120050 recording](https://huggingface.co/datasets/behavior-1k/2025-challenge-rawdata/blob/b3c9a714b8730701c480e77173d8aa4a8f19e1c0/task-0012/episode_00120050.hdf5) (`house_single_floor`, R1Pro, 265 objects), headless, with RGB/depth/normals. Use two wrist cameras at 480×480 and head/left/right external cameras at 320×180. Attach annotators inside `og.sim.editing_usd()`, then call `og.sim.render()`. Each condition below used a fresh process.

| Five-camera configuration | Result |
|---|---|
| `semantic_segmentation` alone | SIGSEGV |
| semantic + instance-ID, at initialization or after warmup | SIGSEGV |
| `instance_segmentation_fast` alone | SIGSEGV |
| `instance_id_segmentation` or `instance_id_segmentation_fast`, without semantic | Completes |

```text
OgnSdInstanceMapping missing valid input renderVar InstanceMappingInfoSDhost
Fatal Python error: Segmentation fault
SyntheticData.py:1504, _post_process_graph_tick -> graph.evaluate()
```

Single-wrist semantic segmentation succeeds. Delayed attachment does not fix the five-camera failure, so this is not simply insufficient warmup.

**Suggested BEHAVIOR workaround:** provide an instance-ID acquisition path that does not automatically enable `seg_semantic`. Resolve each frame's `idToLabels` to mesh/link paths, and explicitly mask missing/`INVALID` entries. Both raw-ID variants produced identical valid-pixel paths in the fixed five-camera test; one view still had 26 invalid foreground pixels out of 57,600. The [Replicator API](https://docs.omniverse.nvidia.com/kit/docs/omni_replicator/1.12.27/source/extensions/omni.replicator.core/docs/API.html#instance-id-segmentation) labels these as development/debugging nodes, so this should remain an explicit fallback rather than silently replacing semantic segmentation.

Please consider documenting this fallback and adding a multi-camera regression test. Mapping readiness and invalid lookup handling also warrant investigation with the renderer upstream. These results do not establish corrupted dataset files or a confirmed native C++ root cause.

Driver 575.64.03 is below the [Isaac 5.1 tested configuration](https://docs.isaacsim.omniverse.nvidia.com/5.1.0/installation/requirements.html) (580.65.06); an updated-driver reproduction remains unverified.
new_candidates.title: Multi-camera segmentation crashes in BEHAVIOR; raw instance-ID workaround

new_candidates.body:
### Description

Headless rendering of a full BEHAVIOR scene segfaults after attaching `semantic_segmentation` or `instance_segmentation_fast` to five cameras. This appears related to [BEHAVIOR-1K #2312](https://github.com/StanfordVL/BEHAVIOR-1K/issues/2312#issuecomment-5013755123), whose maintainers [requested escalation to Isaac](https://github.com/StanfordVL/BEHAVIOR-1K/issues/2312#issuecomment-5027729124).

Tested with R1Pro, `house_single_floor`, 265 objects: two wrist cameras at 480×480 and head/left/right external cameras at 320×180. RGB, depth and normals remain enabled; each condition runs in a fresh process.

| Five-camera condition | Observed result |
|---|---|
| `semantic_segmentation` alone | SIGSEGV |
| semantic + instance-ID, attached during initialization or after warmup | SIGSEGV in both cases |
| `instance_segmentation_fast` alone | SIGSEGV |
| `instance_id_segmentation`, or its `_fast` variant, without semantic | Completes; visible IDs mostly resolve to mesh paths |

A single wrist camera with semantic segmentation succeeds. Thus neither camera count alone nor “all native segmentation is broken” is established.

### Logs

```text
OgnSdInstanceMapping missing valid input renderVar InstanceMappingInfoSDhost
Fatal Python error: Segmentation fault

SyntheticData.py:1504, _post_process_graph_tick -> graph.evaluate()
simulation_context.py:745, render
omnigibson/simulator.py:1188, render
```

### Reproduction

Use the public [2025 challenge raw recording](https://huggingface.co/datasets/behavior-1k/2025-challenge-rawdata/blob/b3c9a714b8730701c480e77173d8aa4a8f19e1c0/task-0012/episode_00120050.hdf5). The following condenses the tested setup; it requires installed OmniGibson assets. Run each annotator in a separate process. The condensed script has not itself been rerun; the table comes from the isolated diagnostic harness with this setup.

<details>
<summary>Scene/camera setup and failing operation</summary>

```python
# python repro.py /path/to/episode_00120050.hdf5 semantic_segmentation
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
import torch
import omnigibson as og
from omnigibson.macros import gm
from omnigibson.envs import HDF5PlaybackWrapper
from omnigibson.utils import transform_utils as T
from isaacsim import SimulationApp

raw, name = sys.argv[1:]
torch.set_num_threads(4)
gm.HEADLESS = True
gm.RENDER_VIEWER_CAMERA = False
gm.USE_GPU_DYNAMICS = False
gm.ENABLE_TRANSITION_RULES = False
SimulationApp.DEFAULT_LAUNCHER_CONFIG['limit_cpu_threads'] = 4
SimulationApp.DEFAULT_LAUNCHER_CONFIG.setdefault('extra_args', []).extend([
    '--/rtx-transient/resourcemanager/enableTextureStreaming=true',
    '--/rtx-transient/resourcemanager/texturestreaming/memoryBudget=0.1',
])
mods = ['rgb', 'depth_linear', 'normal']
head_q = T.quat_multiply(torch.tensor([-1., 0, 0, 0]),
    T.euler2quat(torch.tensor([T.deg2rad(-15.), 0, 0]))).tolist()
mounts = {
    'head': ('zed_link', [.06, 0, .01], head_q, 60.),
    'left': ('base_link', [-.2, .6, 2.], [-.193, .4163, .8062, -.3734], 40.),
    'right': ('base_link', [-.2, -.6, 2.], [.4164, -.1929, -.3737, .8060], 40.),
}
external = [dict(sensor_type='VisionSensor', name=n,
    relative_prim_path=f'/controllable__r1pro__robot_r1/{link}/{n}',
    modalities=mods, sensor_kwargs=dict(image_height=180, image_width=320,
    horizontal_aperture=aperture), position=torch.tensor(pos),
    orientation=torch.tensor(q), pose_frame='parent')
    for n, (link, pos, q, aperture) in mounts.items()]
playback = HDF5PlaybackWrapper.create_from_hdf5(
    input_path=raw, output_path=str(Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'unused.hdf5'),
    robot_obs_modalities=mods,
    robot_sensor_config={'VisionSensor': dict(modalities=mods,
        sensor_kwargs=dict(image_height=480, image_width=480))},
    include_sensor_names=['left_realsense', 'right_realsense'],
    external_sensors_config=external, include_contacts=True,
    include_robot_control=False, include_task=True, include_task_obs=False,
    n_render_iterations=1)
env = playback.env
ext = env.external_sensors
if isinstance(ext, list):
    ext = ext[0]
sensors = [*env.scene.robots[0].sensors.values(), *ext.values()]
for _ in range(8):
    og.sim.render()
import omni.replicator.core as rep
annotators = []
with og.sim.editing_usd():
    for sensor in sensors:
        ann = rep.AnnotatorRegistry.get_annotator(name)
        ann.attach([sensor.render_product])
        annotators.append(ann)
for _ in range(20):
    og.sim.render()  # SIGSEGV for the failing conditions above
    for ann in annotators:
        ann.get_data(device='cpu')
```

</details>

### Workaround and suggested fix

- **Tested workaround:** attach only `instance_id_segmentation`; resolve its per-frame `idToLabels` to mesh/object paths. Explicitly mask missing/`INVALID` mappings instead of treating them as valid objects. In this fixed scene, one view contains 26 such pixels out of 57,600. This is a partial fallback, not an equivalent semantic-segmentation replacement; the [API documents these raw-ID annotators as development/debugging nodes](https://docs.omniverse.nvidia.com/kit/docs/omni_replicator/1.12.27/source/extensions/omni.replicator.core/docs/API.html#instance-id-segmentation).
- **Suggested upstream fix:** validate instance-mapping availability and lookup bounds before semantic/instance reduction; return an explicit invalid result or recoverable error instead of crashing. Investigate render-product mapping initialization in multi-camera scenes. The failure location and related report support this direction, but I have not independently confirmed the native C++ fault.

Is there a fix in a maintained release, or a supported mapping-readiness check for affected versions?

### Environment

- Isaac Sim **5.1.0.0**; Replicator **1.12.27**; SyntheticData **0.6.13**.
- OmniGibson **3.9.3**, Python **3.11.14**. Sensor/annotator implementation unchanged; local device-placement compatibility patches are present.
- Ubuntu **22.04.5**, RTX **5090**, driver **575.64.03**; `nvidia-smi` reports CUDA **12.9**, PyTorch uses CUDA **12.8**.
- Headless, single GPU, CPU PhysX. **Driver limitation:** this is below the **580.65.06** listed in the [5.1 tested configuration](https://docs.isaacsim.omniverse.nvidia.com/5.1.0/installation/requirements.html); an updated-driver/current-release reproduction remains unverified.
